title: Why is this in Spam?
dmarc-fail: It says it's from {domain}, but {domain}'s own security check says they didn't send it.
lying-link: Its links don't go where they say they do.
number-link: Its links go to a bare number instead of a website's name.
fake-name: The sender's name says {detail}, but it wasn't sent by {detail}.
lookalike-domain: It comes from a web address made to look like a different one.
new-domain: It comes from a web address registered in the last month.
spammy-words: It uses words often found in scams and spam.
shouting: Its subject is in capitals or full of exclamation marks.
picture-only: It's almost all pictures, with very little writing.
reply-elsewhere: Your reply would go to a different company from the one that sent it.
advance-fee: It reads like a scam offering money, a prize or an inheritance.
drug-spam: It's selling medicines, as a lot of spam does.
asks-details: It asks you to fill in personal details, such as your address or bank account.
odd-headers: It's missing details that real email programs always add, such as when it was sent.
hidden-recipients: It doesn't say who it was sent to, so it may have gone to thousands of people.
freemail-reply: It's from a company's address, but your reply would go to a free email account.
link-shortener: Its links are hidden behind a link-shortening service.
risky-attachment: It has an attachment that could harm your computer: {detail}.
learnt-spam: It looks like emails you've moved to Spam before.
notSpam: If it's genuine, press Not spam. It moves to your Inbox and mail from this sender won't be checked again. The spam filter learns from it too.
